title: Late Breaking Results: Circuit-Algorithm Co-design for Learnable Audio Analog Front-End
problem: Traditional audio analog front-end design separates circuit design (analog filterbank) from algorithm design (neural network classifier), missing opportunities for joint optimization. The analog filterbank parameters and neural network weights must be co-optimized for better system efficiency and performance.
motivation: Co-optimizing circuits and algorithms can significantly reduce power consumption and silicon area while maintaining classification accuracy for audio processing tasks.
method: The approach jointly trains an audio circuit (source-follower bandpass filter that selects certain sound frequencies) and a Depthwise Separable CNN (a lightweight neural network classifier) as a single system. During training, it uses a combined measurement called Lbpf that weighs both classification accuracy and signal quality (signal-to-noise ratio, or SNR—how much actual signal versus random noise). This shared optimization uses end-to-end backpropagation, which is the standard method for training neural networks but here extended to also adjust the analog circuit parameters, so every component of the system improves together.
key_novelty: The key innovation is jointly optimizing the audio circuit (source-follower bandpass filter) and neural network classifier using SNR-aware training, instead of designing them separately.
contributions: Learnable analog filterbank framework enabling circuit-algorithm co-design
SNR-aware training process with system criterion function combining classification and filter performance
10.6% reduction in bandpass filter power consumption
11.7% chip area reduction while achieving 88.6-94.5% accuracy on 10-keyword classification with 16k parameters
baselines: traditional separate circuit and algorithm design
primary_theme: Circuit-algorithm co-design for efficient audio processing
